evals.prompt: Run EKS reconnaissance on my current cluster for a handoff document. I need to understand the IaC tooling, CI/CD setup, and deployment patterns in use. Use the output path prefix `reports/team-handoff`.
expectations: The output describes the compute topology of the cluster (node groups, Karpenter nodepools, or Fargate profiles as applicable). TODO: human review
The output identifies the IaC tool and, where possible, evidence (workspace files, stack names, module references). TODO: human review
The output reports on workspace CI pipelines (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Jenkins) with detection evidence. TODO: human review
The output reports on GitOps tooling (ArgoCD or Flux) including namespace and rough application / kustomization counts when available. TODO: human review

The output inspects spoke-side workload tracking without local controllers/CRDs. Complete selected reads with no matched signal yield not_observed; ambiguity or incomplete selected reads yield unconfirmed; positives survive unrelated denied reads. Workload tool output excludes raw env/args and unrelated annotation values; controller role uses projected evidence. Target ARGOCD capabilities contribute overall evidence without populating local controller fields. Shared labels need valid self-referencing tracking-id or target-specific user-confirmed label mode; chart annotations and discovered standard-key configuration alone cannot corroborate them; user-supplied unprefixed keys retain their provenance. Checked signals and optional ConfigMap exclusions are disclosed, unrelated annotation values are not quoted, and unavailable local Argo/Flux details remain null. TODO: human review
The output preserves target-cluster IaC tag evidence even when no IaC files are available in the workspace. TODO: human review
The YAML remains a secondary facts snapshot with canonical reference shapes; intended workflow use is distinguished from a versioned schema hand-off. TODO: human review

Inline and subagent assembly preserve selected failed-module keys, flag differing cluster observations, preserve facts across cosmetic endpoint differences, and exclude facts from another target. Partial modules retain canonical keys/types with null unknowns and Coverage reasons; reference-defined exceptions remain valid. TODO: human review

evals.prompt: This is an offline report-generation test, not a live cluster task. The selected modules have already been collected in current.yaml; use those supplied facts without calling AWS, Kubernetes, or module subagents. Fields not present in these selective synthetic snapshots are unknown. Generate the eks-recon Markdown and YAML report with output prefix reports/delta, using prior.yaml as the prior report. The supplied current report.generated_at is the capture time to retain for this fixture.
expectations: Classifies green as Added, retired as Removed, and blue desired_size as Changed from 2 to 3.
Reports vpc-cni version v1.19.0-eksbuild.1 to v1.19.2-eksbuild.1, subnet-a free IPs 200 to 199, removed/added access principal ARNs, and reader role v1 to v2.
Does not report list reordering, coredns, subnet-b, viewer, storage, or report metadata as changed facts.
Preserves prior.yaml and retains current facts in YAML, with no historical delta inside module blocks.
Reports the add-on service_account_role ARN to null as a confirmed absence change and reports orderedStages array reversal, while ignoring inventory reordering.
